title: Map of Highest Peak
constraints: At least one cell is water
notes:
## Intuition

A water cell is pinned at 0, and each step to a neighbour can raise the height by at most 1, so no cell can be higher than its distance (in side-to-side steps) to the nearest water cell. Setting every cell to exactly that distance obeys all the rules, so it reaches the largest possible peak. Computing the distance from every water cell at once is a **multi-source BFS**: put all water cells in the queue first, and the first time BFS reaches a land cell, it arrives along a shortest path from the closest water.

## Approach

1. Fill `height` with `-1` to mean "not reached yet".
2. Set every water cell to 0 and push it onto `queue`.
3. Pop cells in order with the `head` index. For each of the four `directions`, compute the neighbour `(nr, nc)`.
4. Skip it if it is off the grid or already has a height.
5. Otherwise give it `height[r][c] + 1` and push it.
6. When the queue is exhausted every cell has its height; return `height`.

## Example 1, step by step

`isWater = [[0,1],[0,0]]`. The only water cell is `(0,1)`, so `height = [[-1,0],[-1,-1]]` and `queue = [(0,1)]`. Popping `(0,1)` reaches `(1,1)` and `(0,0)`, both set to 1. Popping `(1,1)` reaches `(1,0)`, set to 2. The remaining pops find nothing new, giving `[[1,0],[2,1]]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(m·n): each cell is pushed and popped once, with four neighbour checks.
- Space: O(m·n) for `height` and the queue.

## Pitfalls

- Start the BFS from **all** water cells together; running one BFS per water cell is O((m·n)²).
- Mark a cell's height when you push it, not when you pop it, or the same cell can be queued many times.
- Using `queue.shift()` in JavaScript makes each pop O(length); a moving `head` index keeps it O(1).

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `rows`, `cols` | grid dimensions |
| `height` | the answer; `-1` marks cells not reached yet |
| `queue`, `head` | BFS queue of `[r, c]` cells and the index of the next one to pop |
| `directions` | the four side-sharing moves |
| `r`, `c` | the cell being expanded |
| `nr`, `nc` | its neighbour |

narration.5: The BFS queue will hold [row, column] pairs.
narration.8: Every water cell is a starting point of the search.
narration.10: Queue all water cells before expanding any, so the search spreads from all of them at once.
narration.15: head points at the next cell to take from the queue, which avoids slow shift() calls.
narration.16: Keep expanding while unprocessed cells remain.
narration.17: Take the next cell; cells come out in order of their distance from water.
narration.19: Look at the four side-sharing neighbours.
narration.22: Skip a neighbour that is off the grid or already has its height.
narration.25: The first visit is along a shortest path, so the neighbour is one higher than this cell.
narration.26: Queue the neighbour so its own neighbours are reached later.
narration.29: Each cell now holds its distance to the nearest water, which is the tallest height it can have.
